items.name: FINAL CALL
notes: Gate Change: it trades 1 Front ally with 1 Back ally, pushes both 20 ticks, and leaves FINAL CALL itself Dazzled (1t). If either row has nobody to trade, both allies are still hit and pushed but no one changes row.
Rebooking Stampede: once at 60% HP it calls 1–2 Lost Luggage to the Front and gives every foe +20% Speed (2t, buff), then follows with a party-wide floor sweep.

items.name: Gridlock Prime
notes: Four-Way Red Light: Guard Stance at 30% less damage, plus +30% Def and +25% Atk (2t, buff), and it calls 1 Gridlock, once above and once below 50% HP. Olivia's "Is This Real?" Fact-Check flips the Def buff into a Def penalty.

Overheated Radiator: Exhaust Heatwave leaves Gridlock Prime itself Toasty (2t). A Drench hit sets off Steam Cloud! (3 pips with the Pet Peeve). A Racket hit sets off Panic Boil! and drops Four-Way Red Light.

acts.name: Exhaust Heatwave
acts.effect: Toasty (2t) on allies and on itself.

acts.name: Gridlocked Intersection
acts.effect: Four-Way Red Light, and calls 1 Gridlock.

acts.name: Tinny Shush
acts.effect: Skill Lock (2t). Not on the same ally again for 2 turns.

items.name: Wired Relay Hushling
notes: A Hushling wired to the Drill Worm, in the Back row. It uses the Hushling's acts. HP 400, Atk 104, Def 60, Spd 115, 0 pips, 0 VP. Pet Peeves: Racket, Clobber. Resists: none. While it stands, the Drill Worm takes 25% less damage. Knock it out and the feedback costs the Drill Worm 2 pips and leaves it Dazzled (2t).

items.name: Dual-Coast Drill Worm
notes: Starts with 1 Wired Relay Hushling (see above) and calls one more, once, at 50% HP.
Tunnel Friction Spark leaves the Drill Worm itself Toasty (1t), which a Racket hit turns into Panic Boil!.

acts.name: Tunnel Friction Spark
acts.effect: Toasty (2t) on allies, Toasty (1t) on itself.

acts.name: Relay Call
acts.effect: Once at 50% HP. Calls 1 Wired Relay Hushling.

items.name: The Gold Knight
notes: The chapter's last fight, at the dent in the dome wall. He never speaks. The town's coin is set in his chest plate. The family believes he is the boss, the biggest thing that woke up.
Nobody Rushes Him: he is slow, and above 50% HP nothing pushes him back on the turn bar. This is Boppy's own Boppy Speed trait, and it is the first tell.
Every act is a silent version of something Boppy does. Chapter 14 uses the same seven motions with their real names. No act uses a weapon.
Gold Guard: Guard Stance (2t) while he stands still. Visor Heat leaves him Toasty (2t), so a Racket hit sets off Panic Boil! and drops the guard. Both are his Pet Peeves.

At 0 HP he drops to one knee and the coin falls out of the chest plate. The armor does not break. What follows is a scene, not battle: Grace runs to the dent, a gold hand closes over hers, the helmet opens.

acts.name: Raised Palm
acts.effect: One gold palm up, a short shove. -15% Atk (1t).

acts.name: Slow Walk
acts.effect: He walks in front of the fastest ally and blocks the way. Slow (2t) and a 20-tick push.

acts.name: Wide Arms
acts.effect: He throws both gauntlets wide. The 2nd use hits 3 allies, later uses hit all. A use that reaches every ally counts as aoe.

acts.name: Visor Heat
acts.effect: Heat pours from the visor. Toasty (2t) on allies and on himself.

acts.name: Stand Still
acts.effect: Knees lock, a low rumble comes from the helmet. Gold Guard and Mend 3% (2t).

acts.name: Gold Squeeze
acts.effect: Arms open, he clanks forward and squeezes. Tom's Suite Door Slide can take it.

acts.name: Helmet Hum
acts.effect: Below 50% HP. A long wordless echo. Slow and Fatigue (2t).

items.reward: The town's coin drops, then the scene takes it back

items.name: Boppy's Gold Armor
notes: A normal fight (Tom, 2026-11-17). The party's hits land on the gold armor, never on Boppy. The enemy name says so and the HP bar is labelled as the armor's.

What the player sees on a hit: the helmet flinches, because he feels the knock, and the hit shows as a crack in the gold. Cracks spread in three stages, at 75%, 50% and 25% HP. At 0 HP the armor breaks off him and the battle ends. Everything after that is the scene.

His attacks are normal attacks. They take HP, they can hit Grace and Rose, and the girls hit back. The draft's rule that the girls cannot drop below 1 HP is removed, and so is the adults-only targeting.
Every attack is silly, and none throws or swings a weapon. The draft's halberd is removed.
Nobody Rushes Boppy: slow, and above 50% HP nothing pushes him back on the turn bar.

Resting My Eyes is his Guard Stance. Pepper Breath leaves the armor Toasty (2t), so a Racket hit sets off Panic Boil! and wakes him out of it: the family's noise is the answer, and Sizzle and Racket are both Pet Peeves. Justin's Demo-Day Prybar and a Break also end the guard.

acts.name: "Back Behind the Line!"
acts.effect: Gold palm up, voice booming in the helmet. -15% Atk (1t).

acts.name: "Walk Slower!"
acts.effect: He clanks along beside the fastest ally, complaining. Slow (2t) and a 20-tick push.

acts.name: "It Was THIS Big!"
acts.effect: He throws his arms wide to show the fish and bonks whoever is next to him. The fish grows: 3 allies on the 2nd use, everyone after that. A use that reaches every ally counts as aoe.

acts.name: Pepper Breath
acts.effect: Visor up, one pepper, one big huff. Toasty (2t) on allies and on the armor.

acts.name: Resting My Eyes
acts.effect: The armor locks at the knees and he naps standing up, snoring. Guard Stance and Mend 3% (2t).

acts.name: Great Big Gold Hug
acts.effect: Arms open, he clanks forward and hugs much too hard. Tom's Suite Door Slide can take it.

acts.name: The 1970 Cross-Country Story
acts.effect: Below 50% HP. The 42nd retelling, echoing in the helmet. Slow and Fatigue (2t).

items.reward: The town's coin, handed to Grace by Boppy himself

items.name: The Windowsill Radio
notes: Starts with 2 Hushlings in the Back row as speaker pods (chapter 15 stats, half HP) and calls them back once at 50% HP.
Knocking out a pod sends feedback into the radio: 1 pip and Dazzled (2t).
To keep locks fair: a pod's Tinny Shush cannot hit the same ally twice within 2 turns, and Mute Button has a 2-round wait.

acts.name: Cabinet Thump
acts.effect: The wooden casing hops across the floorboards.

acts.name: Dead Air
acts.effect: Fatigue (1t). At 50% HP it also calls the pods back.

items.name: The Square's Sign
notes: Red-Tape Wall: calls up to 2 Citation Slips to the Back row (404 HP each) and takes Guard Stance at 30% less damage, plus +20% Def (2t, buff). While it lasts, 15% of the damage it takes from any flavor that is not one of its Pet Peeves bounces back at the attacker (rule in 1.1: the attacker cannot be knocked out by it).
Built to be beaten without Deedee and Boppy: Olivia's "Is This Real?" Fact-Check, Justin's Demo-Day Prybar, and a Panic Boil! all open the wall.
items.reward: none: Julian takes the grandparents' coin

items.name: Curator
items.start: White-Glove Protocol: +25% Def and blocks 1 debuff (2t, buff)

items.name: The Twin Lenses
notes: Two stances that swap at each round divider and on Rack Focus. Blue: Pet Peeves Sizzle and Clobber, resists Drench and Razzle. Orange: Pet Peeves Drench and Razzle, resists Sizzle and Racket. It starts Blue.
A Prime put on in one stance can be set off in the next, for example Drenched during Orange, then a Clobber hit in Blue for Hydro-Slip!.
Once at 50% HP it calls 1 Curator to the Front and gains +20% Def (2t, buff).

acts.name: Contact-Sheet Archive
acts.effect: Below 50% HP. Half the power is Sizzle and lands first, half is Drench. Toasty and Drenched (1t).

items.name: The Studio Rig
notes: Spotlight Lock then Big Flash: it locks its lights on one Back-row ally, then fires a flash at that ally on its next turn. Tom's Suite Door Slide takes it, which is the same thing he does in the scene that follows. An interrupt or a Break cancels it.
Once at 50% HP it takes Guard Stance behind a rolled-down backdrop with +20% Atk (2t, buff). The lamps overheat and leave it Toasty (2t), so Panic Boil! brings the backdrop down.

acts.name: Spotlight Lock
acts.effect: Marks the target. It gains +20% Crit Rate (1t, buff).

acts.name: Big Flash
acts.effect: Stun (1t) unless taken by Tom or soaked by a shield.

items.reward: none: the coins go down the mail chute in the scene

items.name: Dead Letter
items.start: Wax-Seal Ward: +20% Def and bounces 1 debuff back (2t, buff)

items.name: Brass Mail-Chute Courier
notes: Mini-boss with Elite stats. No art exists yet.

Wall Perch: it may sit in the Back row even with no foe in Front. It swaps rows every turn with Pneumatic Whoosh: Back for +20% Evasion, Front to land Special Delivery Slam. Pulling it forward or a Break pins it in Front until its next turn.

acts.name: Hot Steam Vent
acts.effect: Toasty (2t) on allies, Toasty (1t) on itself.

acts.name: Special Delivery Slam
acts.effect: Launches from Back to Front. -1 Pep and a 25-tick push.

items.reward: Tom's coin and the grandparents' coin

items.name: The Dead-Letter Censor
notes: REDACTED stamp: from round 2 on, at each round divider it stamps whichever flavor did the most damage to it in the round before. If two flavors tie, or nothing damaged it, it stamps nothing that round. For 1 round, attacks of only that flavor do half damage and take no pips, and the attacker loses 1 Pep after the action (never below 0, and a Basic Action still gains its +2 first). A two-flavor move loses only its matching half (the spec splits such a move half and half). A Break tears the stamp down. The answer is to rotate flavors.
No single-target spikes, because Tom is not there to take them. Pressure is spread across the party so Amy, TNB and Rose can keep everyone up.
Calls 1 Dead Letter (half HP) with Dead-Letter Sort.

acts.name: Dead-Letter Sort
acts.effect: Calls 1 Dead Letter. It gains +20% Def (2t, buff).

acts.name: UNDELIVERABLE
acts.effect: Below 50% HP. Hurricane of stamped mailbags.

items.reward: Clara's coin, inside the returned card

items.name: Blue Lens and Orange Lens
notes: Two lenses it sets in the Back row for phase 2. They do not attack. HP 500 each, Atk 0, Def 75, Spd 115, 0 pips, 0 VP. Pet Peeves: Blue: Sizzle, Clobber. Orange: Drench, Racket. Resists: Blue: Drench, Razzle. Orange: Sizzle, Clobber. While the Blue Lens stands, The Collector takes half damage from Sizzle and Razzle, its own Pet Peeves. While the Orange Lens stands, it takes 25% less damage from everything. With both standing, a Sizzle or Razzle hit is cut by 60%, the spec's cap. Knocking out a lens costs The Collector 2 pips and 5% of its Max HP.

items.name: The Collector
notes: Three phases: 100% to 66%, 65% to 31%, 30% to 0. Damage past a phase line is lost: its HP stops at 66% and at 31%, and the next phase starts at once. The player may pick the 4 again at each change (spec 2.1).

Phase 1, Still Frame: it snapshots where every ally stands on the turn bar. Before or on their next turn, each ally must either be moved on the bar or in the rows (a pull, a push, a swap, a row change or a granted action, from either side) or take part in a Mix or a Detonation. Simply waiting for a turn to come up does not count. An ally who does neither loses 2 Pep and is Slowed (1t).
Phase 2, the lenses: it sets the Blue Lens and the Orange Lens in the Back row (see above). Pulls, party-wide Skills and ranged Skills reach them.

Phase 3, the countdown: it refills all 8 pips, drops its resistances and counts down 200 ticks (two round dividers) to one huge flash. Break it before the count ends and the flash never fires. Only a Break stops the count: interrupt Skills do not cancel this one. A Full Family Ruckus takes 4 pips in one action, which makes it the tool for this.

acts.name: Lens Set
acts.effect: Start of phase 2. Sets both lenses.

acts.name: Countdown
acts.effect: Start of phase 3. Refills 8 pips, 200-tick count. Only a Break cancels it.

acts.name: The Biggest Picture
acts.effect: Fires if the count ends unbroken. -3 Pep and Slow (2t).

items.name: BAG command and Run
items.plain: The fourth button on the command cross is greyed in the new battle. In battle 2 it opened the bag and let the party run. The plan keeps both: items re-described with the new statuses, and Run in fights that allow it. No stage in the plan owns it yet.
items.source: claude/battle-architecture.md gap table rows 26 and 30; the game: the BAG button says "Not yet"

items.name: Tombo skins on the Full Family Ruckus
items.plain: The 22 Primary Tombos (named pair moves with a spoken line and an animation, from battle 2) come back as optional skins: when Tom and a partner fire a Full Family Ruckus, the skin gives the name, the line and the animation. The result stays the rule's (both fire their best Skill) and a skin carries no numbers. A Move Lab review (Keep, Tweak, Replace) decides which skins make the cut. Until then no Tombo shows in the new battle, and the Tombo unlock flags are still saved.
items.source: claude/battle-architecture.md section 3 and stage 16; docs/BATTLE3.md (Tombo toasts)

items.name: Casual Mode (Freelancer)
items.plain: The endgame reward, around chapter 18. A person unlocks it by mastering all three of their Vibes. It is a fourth Vibe with no Skills of its own and no Stat Lean. As Main Vibe it gives two Pocket Vibe slots instead of one, the Basic Action of the player's choice from that person's Vibes, and all three of that person's Traits. With every Vibe mastered there is no Vibe Point left to earn, which the game already handles.

items.name: Knocked-out members stand up at 1 HP after a win
items.plain: The spec says a member who is knocked out when a fight is won stands back up at 1 HP. In a story fight the new battle hands HP back to the map as a share of Max HP, so a member who ended the fight knocked out stays at 0 HP.
items.source: claude/battle-spec-v11.md section 2.9; claude/battle-architecture.md gap row 25; engine/b3-story.js b3sEnd

items.name: Gear counts in fights
items.plain: Stat bonuses from gear and Charms should pass through a mapping table in data (POW to Attack, GRIT to Defense, PEP to Speed, HP to HP), with perks that have no meaning in the new rules switched off in that table. The new battle reads no gear today: its stats come from the level table, the Lean and the Vibes.

items.name: Helper links and helper feedback
items.plain: A boss that calls helpers (chapter 15 speaker pods, chapter 16 Citation Slips, chapter 20) takes less damage while a helper stands, and loses pips and HP when a helper is knocked out. The pips count inside the 3-pip cap of the action that did it; the HP is a flat amount with no modifiers.
items.source: claude/bestiary-v11.md section 1.1 (Helper links, Helper feedback); engine/b3-foe.js header

items.name: The Twin Lenses stances
items.plain: Chapter 17's boss has two stances that swap at every round divider and on Rack Focus. Blue hates Sizzle and Clobber and resists Drench and Razzle; Orange hates Drench and Razzle and resists Sizzle and Racket. A Prime put on in one stance can be set off in the next.

items.name: Boss phases and phase lines
items.plain: The last boss has three phases (100% to 66%, 65% to 31%, 30% to 0). Damage past a phase line is lost: its HP stops at the line and the next phase starts at once. Boppy's Gold Armor in chapter 14 also shows cracks at 75%, 50% and 25% HP.
items.source: claude/bestiary-v11.md section 1.1 (Phase lines) and chapters 14 and 20; engine/b3-foe.js header

items.name: Pick the four again at each phase of the last fight
items.plain: The party is four, and swapping happens outside battle only, with one exception: in the last fight the player picks the four again at each phase change. A person coming in for the first time arrives at full HP with 4 Pep; one who was in it earlier returns with the HP and Pep they left with. Everyone joins the turn bar waiting 100 x 100 / Speed ticks.

items.name: Part 1 monsters come back in chapters 13 and 14
items.plain: The Long Island monsters the family met in Part 1 return in chapters 13 and 14 as returning packs and bosses, drawn larger with a brighter palette on the Part 1 art. Which places return is set by the chapter 13 and 14 scripts.

items.name: Tombo skins
items.plain: A Move Lab review of the 22 Primary Tombos (Keep, Tweak or Replace), then the kept ones wired onto the Full Family Ruckus as named skins with their recorded line.

items.name: Third Vibes and Casual Mode
items.plain: The ten third Vibes, three or four people per conversation, then Casual Mode. At the end all 30 Vibes are in the game and each person can be Main in any of three jobs. They show in the Family tab as PLANNED until then.

items.name: The Part 2 chapters, 11 to 20
items.plain: Each chapter's monsters and boss are built inside that chapter's own story build, one chapter per conversation, with the helper links, the lenses, the phase lines and picking the four again where a chapter needs them. A chapter goes on the new battle only after its fights pass in the Battle Lab and its chapter test passes.

items.name: The purge
items.plain: Battle 2 is deleted: the old battle files, Stampcards, Kindness in battle, the Director's Cuts, the Family Finishes, unused voice lines and clips, the old Lab fights and old docs. Nothing new to see; the game is smaller and loads faster.
